rounds.notes:
INTERIM RECORD, pending independent re-review: the reviewer seat is out (owner decision 31 Oct 2026), so this record is signed with the interim reviewer key on the owner's standing decision, and the contract it makes signable waits for an independent re-review. The review was a red-team read of pull request #382 at head d396c64 (spec hash af608dcd529b), made before this record, and the signer confirmed that the head and its spec bytes are the ones reviewed. It read the whole spec and found no blocking finding.
What the review ran: the five labelled subtests were written and run at the pinned base 2f24e94 in a scratch worktree, and for the green half a change of policy.mjs that follows the five requirements. Red: T1-c01 to T1-c04 each fail on code: 'ERR_ASSERTION' at the base (not a load error or TypeError, the modules are reached by namespace import with a typeof guard); T1-c05 passes at the base and with the change, as the spec says. Green: all five pass with the change. Mutants: dropping the party filter fails c01, c02 and c03; putting deny.not_a_party first in DENY_RULES fails c01; echoing the node in the reason fails c01; a gate that passes no node fails c01, c02 and c03. The manifest row states 17 criteria and the spec has 17, no command pipes through tail or head, every command parses with sh -n, the grep of criterion 9 does not match the base, the docs sentence and list item that criterion 8 removes exist at the base, and the scope is policy.mjs, the new test, docs/FEDERATION.md and the changelog entry. The gate --report on main merged with the pull request shows 0 NOT SIGNABLE and only SO-F-04C as NO RECORD; the history leak scan is clean. Criterion 6 (test/membership.test.mjs) could not be run to green on this box: its three end-to-end subtests need OpenSSH 8.0 and fail the same way at the base; by reading, their contributions come from node-a against a relationship of node-a and node-b, so they stay admitted. I did not run npm test.
Non-blocking notes for the builder: (1) no criterion has a node that is a party of a relationship of another scope: a change that counts such a relationship (a party match that ignores the scope) passes all five subtests, so add the case to c01 or c03: a node that is a party only in another scope is refused with deny.not_a_party when some relationship covers the scope, and with deny.no_relationship when none does; (2) criterion 4 lists 'or a string' among the bad nodes, which reads as a valid node, so it should say an envelope that is a string; (3) the spec says 'non-empty text' for the node while a party node is an id of at most 128 characters of letters, digits and . _ : -, so say whether a longer or odd node is bad_request or not_a_party, and test one; (4) deny.not_a_party against deny.no_relationship tells a sender whether any relationship covers a scope, which is acceptable only if refusals are not returned to the sender; (5) criteria 10 and the scope criterion hold only on a branch that starts at 2f24e94 and has not merged main when verify runs; (6) criterion 6 depends on the box having OpenSSH 8.0 or later; (7) whether evaluate treats a node key that is present but undefined as no node should be said (the change refuses it as bad_request). No finding is open.

answers.how: No criterion has a node that is a party of a relationship of another scope. Requirement 1 limits the relationships considered to those valid for the scope, but every fixture of c1 to c5 holds one scope: c1 has one relationship, c2 has two live relationships of the same scope, c3 has a live relationship of the same scope beside the refused one, and c5 has no node. A build whose party match ignores the scope, so that it admits a node that is a party only of another scope's relationship whenever some relationship covers the scope, passes all five subtests and c7. That is the authorisation check this contract adds. A criterion that catches it: with a live relationship of node-a and node-b for scope S1 and a live relationship of node-x and node-y for scope S2, a contribution for S1 from node-x is refused with deny.not_a_party, and a contribution from node-x for a scope S3 that no relationship covers is refused with deny.no_relationship; the test fails before the change on an assertion and passes after. Round 1 recorded this as its builder note 1 and raised no answer.

folded_as.statement: A node that is a party only of another scope's relationship is not a party of this scope: with a live relationship of node-a and node-b for scope S1 and a live relationship of node-x and node-y for scope S2 (the subject a member of both), a contribution for S1 from node-x is refused with ok false and the code deny.not_a_party while node-a and node-b are admitted for S1, node-x is admitted for S2, and a contribution from node-x for a scope S3 that no relationship covers is refused with deny.no_relationship. The test fails before the change on an assertion and passes after

answers.how: Requirement 1 says a node must be a non-empty text, otherwise deny.bad_request. A party node is an id of 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits and . _ : - (ID_RE in src/engine/federation/membership.mjs). The spec does not say which refusal a node gets that is a non-empty text and not a valid id, such as one of 129 characters or one holding a space, and no criterion has one. By the letter of requirement 1 it is not deny.bad_request, so it is deny.not_a_party or deny.no_relationship; a build that answers deny.bad_request for it passes every subtest. The refusal code is what other nodes will code against. Say which refusal it is and pin one such node in c4 or c1.

folded_as.statement: A node that is a non-empty text and not a node id is no party's node: against a live relationship of node-a and node-b for the scope (the subject a member), a node of 129 characters and a node holding a space are each refused with ok false and the code deny.not_a_party, never deny.bad_request, and the refusal holds neither node; for a scope that no relationship covers each is refused with deny.no_relationship. The test fails before the change on an assertion and passes after

answers.how: Criterion 4 lists 'null, undefined or a string' after the bad nodes. It means an envelope that is null, undefined or a string. As written it reads as a node that is a string, which requirement 1 accepts. Say 'an envelope that is null, undefined or a string'.

folded_as.statement: An envelope with no origin, an origin with no node, a node that is not a text or an empty node, and an envelope that is itself null, undefined or a string, is refused with ok false and the code deny.bad_request, the refusal holds no payload, and the gate does not throw. The test fails before the change (the contribution passes) on an assertion and passes after

answers.how: The request ends 'Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: ... there is no Federated tier.' Pull request 403 of 2 November 2026 introduced the Federated tier as a planned fifth tier, so main now contradicts the clause. It decides nothing in this contract. Remove it, or date it so the spec does not state as current something main has changed.
answers.reason: No criterion is added, because no criterion checks the request. The clause is removed from the request in this fold, as the answer asks.

rounds.notes: INDEPENDENT RE-REVIEW by the reviewer seat, signed with the reviewer key 1f6b4e7c00729bc7, of the spec as it is on main at 6fba2fa38eff41bc328b6c747483dd92c22032c2. It re-reviews round 1, the interim solo record. This is a re-issue of round 2 before landing: its first version (commit 1e9dbec9d35c88ac883e5bd0505c35734796c7c5 on the review branch, never landed) raised no answer and did not rule on the seven builder notes of round 1, and the lead's review of it showed that the first of those notes is a way for a broken build to pass. 1. Why this round: round 1 reviewed at 2f24e942, and docs/FEDERATION.md, which is in the scope, then changed in 1df013d (pull request 388, before the signing commit 461d4834), 080eedd and 8d418db, so the gate reported head_stale_src and the suite's T2-c01 failed on main. 2. What was read: the whole spec (request, T1, its six requirements and seventeen criteria), the snapshot of round 1 and the notes of round 1 in full. The spec is unchanged since round 1 (canonical hash af608dcd529b). The three source inputs of round 1 (policy.mjs, membership.mjs, admission.mjs) are byte-identical at 6fba2fa3. docs/FEDERATION.md was read in full at 6fba2fa3, together with its diff from 2f24e942. 3. The FEDERATION.md drift does not touch what the spec asks for: requirement 5 and c8 need the page to name deny.not_a_party and to lose the line 'Binding the sending node in the gate' and the policy.mjs comment 'does not yet bind the sending node'; both are still present at 6fba2fa3, so c8 is red before the build as it should be, and the lines added since round 1 match neither of c8's patterns. 4. Rulings on the seven builder notes that round 1 recorded. Its first note is answer 1, high. Its third note is answer 2, medium. Its second note is answer 3, low. Its fourth note (deny.not_a_party against deny.no_relationship tells whoever sees a refusal whether a relationship covers the scope) stays a note: a correct build has this property, no criterion in this task's scope can check what a transport returns, and Admission returns a refusal to its local caller today; it wants an open row in the register so the transport contract takes it up. Its fifth note (c10 and the scope criterion hold only on a branch cut from the pinned base that has not merged main) stays a note: the spec pins the base in c11, and seven files of src and scripts changed on main after it (scripts/license/issue.mjs, src/cli/main.mjs, src/cli/sync.mjs, src/cli/work-store.mjs, src/engine/entitlements.mjs, src/engine/paid-merge.mjs, src/engine/vault.mjs), so the builder cuts the branch from 2f24e942 and verifies before any merge of main. Its sixth note (c6 needs OpenSSH 8.0 or later) stays a note about the machine. Its seventh note (a node key that is present and undefined) stays a note: c4 pins the gate's refusal of an envelope with no origin.node whichever way evaluate reads an undefined node, so no broken gate passes on it. 5. Answer 4 is new in this round: the request's closing sentence on the tiers. 6. Requirements against criteria: requirement 1 is checked by c1, c2, c3 and c5 except for its restriction to the scope, which is answer 1; requirement 2 by c4 and c2; requirement 3 by c1; requirement 4 by c2 and c3; requirement 5 by c8; requirement 6 by c10. Each red-green criterion (c1 to c4) runs only its own labelled subtest of its own test file. Verdict: findings.

answers.how: Requirement 1 says a node in the request must be a non-empty text, otherwise deny.bad_request, and requirement 2 has the gate refuse an envelope with no usable origin.node itself. Every criterion that sends a bad node (criterion 4) goes through relationshipGate, and criterion 5 calls evaluate() only with no node or with a valid one. A build whose gate refuses a bad node on its own, and whose evaluate() treats a node that is present and not a non-empty text (null, a number, an empty text) as no node, passes every criterion; for such a request evaluate() then decides as at the base and can allow. The spec also does not say whether a node key that is present and undefined counts as no node. relationshipGate is the only caller today, so no shipped path reaches this. A criterion that catches it: in criterion 5, evaluate() with node null, 5 and an empty text each returns deny.bad_request, and the spec says which way an undefined node is read. This refines my round 2 ruling on round 1's seventh note, which I kept as a note because criterion 4 pins the gate.
answers.reason: Not added as a criterion in this version. relationshipGate is the only caller of evaluate() in src at main 6fba2fa3, and criterion 4 pins the gate's refusal of every bad node, so no shipped path reaches evaluate() with one. Requirement 1 still requires deny.bad_request. The case stays open as issue 410 of the memev repository, to be pinned when evaluate() gains a second caller or when this contract is next amended; the build's own subtest T1-c04 may assert it directly.

rounds.notes: INDEPENDENT REVIEW by the reviewer seat, signed with the reviewer key 1f6b4e7c00729bc7, of the folded spec at commit 775e78fc63c7f7484aca534468167e318c7bdb6f (canonical hash 4dbeff09bd9a). 1. What was read: the whole folded spec and its difference from the round 2 snapshot, which is exactly this: requirement 1 reworded, criterion 4 reworded, criterion 7 naming two more subtests in its statement and in its command, criteria 18 and 19 added, and the clause on the Federated tier removed from the request. Nothing else changed, and no requirement or criterion was removed. policy.mjs, membership.mjs and admission.mjs were read at 775e78fc. 2. What was run, in a scratch worktree at the pinned base 2f24e942 with a probe test of my own that states criteria 18 and 19 as the spec does: at the base both fail on an assertion (ERR_ASSERTION, not a load error); with a change that follows the requirements both pass, and test/membership.test.mjs passes all twelve of its tests with that change; a build whose party match ignores the scope fails criterion 18 and passes criterion 19; a build that answers deny.bad_request for a node that is no node id passes criterion 18 and fails criterion 19; so each new criterion is red before, green after, and catches the build it was added for. 3. The builder's decision on the second answer of round 2 (a node that is a text and no node id is refused as any node that is no party) is sound: evaluate considers only records that pass validateRelationship, which requires each party's node to match the id rule, so such a node equals no party's node; the other choice would need the id rule inside policy.mjs, which requirement 6 keeps free of new imports. 4. Dispositions of round 2: its first and second answers are added word for word as criteria 18 and 19; its third answer is added as the reworded criterion 4, which names the same cases; its fourth answer adds no criterion and its clause is removed from the request, as the fold's difference shows. 5. The four amendments of this round were each checked against the round 2 snapshot and the folded spec: requirement 1 gains two restrictions, criterion 4 is clarified with its cases unchanged, and criterion 7 gains the two new subtests in its statement and its command. Each tightens or clarifies, and none loosens. 6. One answer of severity low is raised, on evaluate() when it is called directly; it refines my round 2 ruling on the seventh builder note that round 1 recorded. 7. Notes for the builder and the signer, not answers: the manifest row's status text still describes the signing of 1 November and wants updating when version 2 is signed; this round reviewed commit 775e78fc, so the landing keeps that commit as an ancestor of the signing commit; docs/FEDERATION.md is in the scope, so another change to it on main before the landing makes the record stale again; and the round 2 rulings on the fourth, fifth and sixth builder notes of round 1 stand. Verdict: clean, with no high answer.

amendments.from: evaluate(request, ...) accepts an optional node in the request. With no node in the request every result is exactly what it is at the base. With a node: it must be a non-empty text, otherwise deny.bad_request; the relationships considered are those valid for the scope that name the node as a party; if none is valid for the scope the denial is deny.no_relationship; if some are and none names the node it is deny.not_a_party; otherwise the existing evaluation (live, revoked, expired, not yet established, policy version, class rule, action) runs over the relationships that name the node (source: src/engine/federation/policy.mjs, evaluate, as merged by pull request #368)
amendments.to: evaluate(request, ...) accepts an optional node in the request. With no node in the request every result is exactly what it is at the base. With a node: it must be a non-empty text, otherwise deny.bad_request; the relationships considered are those valid for the scope that name the node as a party; if none is valid for the scope the denial is deny.no_relationship; if some are and none names the node it is deny.not_a_party; a relationship of another scope never counts, so a node that is a party only of another scope's relationship is refused as any node that is no party; a node that is a non-empty text and not a node id (the id rule of memev-membership/1: 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits and . _ : -) is no party's node, so it is refused in the same way, with deny.not_a_party or deny.no_relationship and never with deny.bad_request; otherwise the existing evaluation (live, revoked, expired, not yet established, policy version, class rule, action) runs over the relationships that name the node (source: src/engine/federation/policy.mjs, evaluate, as merged by pull request #368)
